children: Max Smart Super Speciality Hospital in Saket has added a 400-bed tower, taking its total capacity to around 1,200 beds and making it the largest private hospital in Delhi by bed capacity, according to Max Healthcare.

Union Home Minister and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah inaugurated the new tower at the hospital in New Delhi on Thursday, September 3. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, Health and Family Welfare Minister Pankaj Kumar Singh and South Delhi MP Ramvir Singh Bidhuri attended the event.

The expansion will strengthen the hospital's ability to provide tertiary and quaternary care across more than 22 specialities. The company said the new facility is aimed at meeting the growing demand for specialised healthcare in Delhi-NCR and beyond.
New tower adds advanced surgical technology
The new facility houses the Da Vinci Xi Surgical Robot and Mako Total Knee Replacement Robot, which Max Healthcare said will support minimally invasive procedures across multiple specialities.

Commenting on the inauguration, Abhay Soi, Chairman and Managing Director of Max Healthcare Institute, said, “This state-of-the-art new facility brings together cutting-edge technology, world-class infrastructure and exceptional Indian clinical talent to deliver advanced, high-quality patient care to people from India and across the globe.”
He added that the facility “contributes to the broader vision of building a stronger and inclusive healthcare ecosystem in India” and supports the country's journey towards a Viksit Bharat.

Max Healthcare said it treated more than 40 lakh patients from over 800 cities and 180 countries in the last financial year. The company operates 21 healthcare facilities with more than 6,100 beds, according to the release.

It also said it provided free treatment worth ₹244 crore to 3.60 lakh patients last year. Its Max Institute of Medical Sciences has supported 1.62 lakh students through higher education, training and professional learning programmes.

The company reported its first-quarter earnings in August, with net profit rising 3% to ₹357 crore from ₹345 crore in the year-ago period. Revenue increased 15.2% to ₹2,835 crore from ₹2,460 crore, while EBITDA rose 15% to ₹704 crore from ₹613 crore. EBITDA margin, however, contracted marginally to 24.8% from 24.9%.
Max Healthcare's board also approved a capital expenditure of ₹425 crore to set up an additional hospital block and gave in-principle approval for setting up medical colleges or medical institutions.
Shares of the company were trading at ₹992.20, down 0.18% from their previous close.

title: Max Healthcare’s Saket hospital adds 400 bed tower, takes capacity to 1,200
